newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends with strong gains, soyoil slips.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends with strong gains, soyoil slips.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended with sharp gains on Tuesday amid aggressive commercial buying, pit sources said.
Soyoil again faltered, pressured by ideas soymeal demand would lead to increased production while soyoil usage remained stagnant.

The May soymeal contract climbed back above the $300 per ton mark, leading that market higher on ideas processors would continue to hold tightly to deliverable supplies. Trade sources noted cash soymeal was trading at a premium to futures, making it unattractive for commercials to deliver.

Continental Grain was a strong buyer of soymeal on the day while ADM and Cargill were also on the buy side. The moves raised suspicions of export business in the works but exporters could not confirm any trades.
Soymeal and soyoil had faltered earlier in the session amid news soybean crusher Owensboro Grain Co confirmed it was negotiating to buy more soybeans from South America.
The company would not confirm tonnage but other U.S. exporters said the deal involved up to two cargoes.
Soymeal ended $5.90 to $1.80 per ton higher while soyoil closed 0.08 cent per lb lower to 0.02 cent higher.

Weather was also deemed supportive. Forecasts called for a cool week in the U.S. Midwest which could hamper plantings. Trade sources also cited talk a U.S. analytical firm had cut its projection for 1997 U.S. soybean acreage.
The market had collapsed on Monday after USDA projected record new crop soybean production.

Commercials provided support for soymeal and soyoil throughout the session. On the day, Continental Grain bought at least 700 lots July soymeal and 200 lots December. Cargill Inc bought 200 July and ADM bought 100 July.
Merrill Lynch sold 800 July and SAK Futures sold 600 July, pit sources said.
In soyoil, Cargill bought 500 July and ADM bought 200 July and sold 700 July. FIMAT Futures and E.D. and F. Man International each sold 300 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 34,822 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, against Monday's actual 17,443 lots.
